01Finished outputs

Open the finished files.

One public Bologna record: 19 interviews, 317 defined codes and 874 codings. These files come from the workbench’s existing exporters.

01 / CODED SOURCE

Tree Notebook

Full interview02.txt text, 53 saved codings, highlights and their tree paths.

Read Notebook ↗Editable Word ↓
Source scope & tree labels

18,239 characters. Explicit display convention: root Theme, intermediate Category, leaf Code. Saved names and links are unchanged.

02 / RESEARCH WRITING

Research report

Qualitative Content Analysis, method map, an Analysis Table, illustrative Narrative Analysis and five figures.

Read report ↗Editable Word ↓Complete report ZIP ↓
03 / FIGURES AND RECIPES

Five figures. Exact counts.

SVG, PDF and 300 dpi PNG for each figure, with its CSV and standalone Python script. Extract the ZIP before running the code.

Explore figures ↓Five figures & code ZIP ↓
04 / CONTINUE THE PROJECT

Restore in your workspace

Project JSON preserves all 19 source documents, original coding and the saved example report. Restore it as a new project in your private online account, or use the local workspace.

Project JSON ↓Local setup ↗

Illustrative writing from existing codes; not a newly validated research analysis. Word text and tree labels are editable; editing Word does not update QT. The five figures cover the whole corpus; the Notebook covers one complete interview. File hashes & source record ↗

Interpretation & limits

The final exported point is 259 distinct codes encountered across 19 interviews, compared with 317 codes defined in the full codebook.

The route through the curve depends on the order of the files. A slower rise alone does not decide whether the research is complete. Finish with the counting rules and export record.

08Methods & limits

This worked example describes existing coding counts. For your own Research report, select one method in Export: Thematic Analysis, Qualitative Content Analysis or Qualitative Comparative Analysis. Its saved name and process map accompany HTML, editable Word and the report ZIP. Explore the three method maps.

Follow each number back to its export.

The page reads the workbench’s SVGs and CSVs. It checks every listed file against the manifest’s SHA-256 and byte length before showing the report. Count tables retain the exported rows and order. The unit statements below come directly from that same manifest.

Counting rules from the manifest
Code frequency
Counts passage-code assignments, not participants. Frequency is not importance.
Code × interview
Counts passage-code assignments, not participants. Zero means no coding in this interview.
Co-occurrence heatmap
Codes whose character ranges overlap within one interview. Descriptive; not correlation.
Theme hierarchy
Counts coded extracts per section and subsection, not participants.
Code accumulation
Interviews in file-name order, not the order conducted. A plateau is not saturation.
